demographics.trauma_type: Accidentally caused serious injury to another

Memory.value: I know what happened but I am unable to find words to describe it
When I remember the frightening event I feel like it is happening right now.
The memory is so extreme it is hard to believe it actually happened to me

vignette: Mohammad is a 78-year-old Middle Eastern man who has been struggling with intrusive memories and emotional triggers following an accident that caused serious injury to a colleague at work. Mohammad works as an environmental scientist and the event occurred during a routine field study in a remote forest area. The day of the incident was initially uneventful, but it took a tragic turn when Mohammad accidentally knocked over a heavy rock while trying to secure equipment for a soil sample test. The rock fell onto his colleague's leg, causing severe injuries that required immediate medical attention. Since then, Mohammad has been haunted by flashbacks and intense emotional triggers. One of the most potent triggers for Mohammad is hearing heavy breathing sounds. Whenever he hears someone breathe heavily—whether it’s during a workout at the gym or when he sees people exert themselves—he is immediately transported back to that moment in the forest. He recounts feeling like he can still hear his colleague's labored breaths as they waited anxiously for an ambulance to arrive. This auditory trigger often causes him to relive the event, and he describes it as if he were right there again, unable to escape the horror of what happened. Additionally, feelings of happiness or relaxation also serve as triggers that can set off his intrusive memories. Mohammad had initially planned a family gathering at their home but found himself overwhelmed by a sense of unease when his children and grandchildren started laughing and enjoying themselves. The joyous atmosphere was a stark contrast to the fear he experienced during the accident, and he often felt guilty for not being able to enjoy these moments without intrusive thoughts. Physical affection such as hugs from his wife can also trigger memories that Mohammad finds almost unbearable. He remembers how comforting it would be when they hugged after long days at work before the incident. Now, such intimate moments only serve to remind him of the fragility of life and his role in causing harm. Mohammad often struggles with describing what happened precisely, despite knowing the details vividly. The memory is so extreme that he finds it difficult to believe it actually occurred to him. He describes how the event feels surreal, almost like a dream, yet the pain and guilt are real and constant. When he tries to recount the incident to his wife or during counseling sessions, he often stumbles over his words, feeling as though they cannot adequately convey the depth of what he experienced. One day, after an especially distressing flashback triggered by heavy breathing sounds at work, Mohammad realized that these memories were beginning to affect his ability to perform his job effectively. He found himself increasingly distracted and anxious, making simple tasks seem insurmountable. His colleagues noticed a change in his behavior but were unaware of the root cause. It was during one particularly intense episode while working on a report that he broke down at his desk. Feeling both overwhelmed and embarrassed, Mohammad knew then that he could no longer handle these symptoms alone. What finally brought him to seek help was not just the intensity of his symptoms but the fear that they would continue to erode his professional life as well. Mohammad is most afraid of being seen as responsible for the accident, a constant weight on his mind that disrupts his peace and happiness. However, he also hopes for relief from these overwhelming memories and triggers so he can return to enjoying time with his family without intrusive thoughts. He seeks therapy to better understand how to manage these feelings and regain control over his life. Through this journey, Mohammad hopes to find a way to process the trauma and learn coping mechanisms that will allow him to live more fully without being haunted by the past.
